Yes. Several papers support dynamically changing how many pages are fetched at test time without retraining: ViSAR is a training-free adaptive-k method that dynamically determines the number of pages to retrieve [1], and LAD-RAG dynamically adapts retrieval with an LLM agent without top-k tuning [2]. LITTA also improves retrieval without retriever retraining, with the number of query variants controlling the accuracy-efficiency trade-off [6].

If you want the closest match to “how many pages are fetched,” [1] and [2] are the most direct; [9] also dynamically reallocates retrieval budgets toward high-value query aspects, but it focuses on aspect-aware subqueries rather than a simple page-count rule [9].
